strategies.name: Irrigation System Audit & Leak Repair
strategies.description: Professional audit of pumps, pipes, fittings and outlets to identify and fix leaks, pressure loss, and uneven distribution. Usually the first, cheapest step before any capital investment.
strategies.source: EPA WaterSense; general industry consensus that inefficient/leaking systems waste up to 50% of applied water to evaporation, runoff, and leakage

strategies.name: Soil Moisture Sensor Network + Scheduling
strategies.description: Capacitive or tensiometer-based soil moisture sensors feeding an irrigation scheduling dashboard, replacing calendar-based or rule-of-thumb watering.
strategies.source: Multi-study synthesis: soil moisture sensors show water savings of at least 15% (up to 50%+ in favorable deployments); conservative field trials on high-value crops (strawberry/almond) show 10-16% with yield maintained

strategies.name: Evapotranspiration (ET)-Based Scheduling Subscription
strategies.description: Software service that uses BoM weather/ET data plus crop coefficients to recommend irrigation timing and volume. No hardware install required.
strategies.source: Comparable to sensor-scheduling literature but lower savings ceiling since it doesn't measure actual in-field soil state; positioned as a lower-cost entry point

strategies.name: Mulching / Crop Residue Retention
strategies.description: Retaining stubble or applying organic mulch to reduce surface evaporation and improve soil water holding capacity.
strategies.source: General agronomic literature on evaporation reduction via surface cover; not applicable to flood/paddy systems where residue interferes with water flow

strategies.name: Laser Land Leveling
strategies.description: Precision grading of flood/furrow-irrigated fields to a uniform micro-gradient, eliminating pooling and uneven advance. Typically contracted, redone every 3-5 years as soil moves.
strategies.source: Converging estimates of 20-30% water consumption reduction across multiple field studies; older benchmark work (Bhatt & Sharma 2009) reports 25-30% without yield penalty

strategies.name: Targeted Drip/Micro-Irrigation Conversion
strategies.description: Converting the highest-value or most water-stressed 25% of irrigated area (not the whole farm) from flood/spray to drip. Capital cost and savings are scaled to that fraction only, reflecting realistic partial-adoption economics.
strategies.source: Solid-set/pipe systems ~90% efficiency vs 75% flood (Agriculture Victoria); drip broadly reported at 30-60% savings vs flood. Conservative end used, applied to 25% of farm area only

strategies.name: Travelling Gun to Solid-Set/Pipe & Riser Upgrade
strategies.description: Replacing travelling-gun or hand-move sprinklers with fixed solid-set or pipe-and-riser systems, which have meaningfully higher application efficiency.
strategies.source: Agriculture Victoria (2003): solid-set/pipe & riser ~90% efficiency vs 65-75% for travelling gun systems

strategies.name: On-Farm Tailwater Recycling Pit
strategies.description: Small farm-scale catchment pit and pump-back system to capture and reuse irrigation runoff/tailwater, rather than losing it off-property.
strategies.source: Placeholder estimate — needs validation against regional case studies (e.g. NSW DPI or Cotton Australia tailwater return system reports); not independently verified in this pass

strategies.name: Remote Telemetry & Automated Pump Shutoff
strategies.description: Remote monitoring and automated cutoff of pumps/channels to prevent overnight or unattended over-application.
strategies.source: Placeholder estimate based on general automation-reduces-overwatering logic — needs validation against vendor case studies

strategies.name: Soil Amendment (Gypsum / Organic Matter)
strategies.description: Improving soil structure and water-holding capacity via gypsum application (for sodic/clay soils) or organic matter incorporation, reducing irrigation frequency.
strategies.source: Placeholder estimate — soil-specific; only effective on sodic/clay-heavy soils, needs regional soil-survey validation before presenting as a firm figure

strategies.name: Managed Deficit Irrigation (Agronomist-Supervised)
strategies.description: Controlled, science-based under-watering at non-critical crop growth stages, run with agronomist supervision to protect yield. Near-zero capital cost but requires ongoing expert input.
strategies.source: Deficit irrigation studies on citrus/cotton report 10-20% savings with acceptable yield trade-off when properly managed; unmanaged deficit irrigation carries real yield risk and is why this requires agronomist supervision

strategies.name: On-Farm Supply Channel to Pipe Conversion
strategies.description: Converting open on-farm delivery channels (not shared/community infrastructure) to piped delivery, cutting conveyance loss to evaporation and seepage. Highest capital tier in this catalog — only economically sound for larger operations with significant channel length.
strategies.source: General conveyance-loss literature for open channel vs piped delivery; needs regional cost validation before use in client-facing figures
